_what: Seven Days to the Wolves — the whole programme, assembled from its acts. THE RUNNING ORDER IS CANONICAL and settled by the owner on 2026-08-12: intro (I) -> endlessformsmostbeautiful (II) -> mrbobbytables (III) -> kat (IV) -> nat (V) -> 7daystothewolves (VI) -> europa (VII) -> credits (VIII). docs/running-order.md is the source of truth for it; this file executes it.

_acts.I: intro — the Into the Light opener, six Guardians plated, with the title cover (wolves.jpg) covering source 24.5 - 38.
_acts.II: endlessformsmostbeautiful — delivered and credited, in the programme. Five unbroken runs of the live-action trailers scored to Nightwish's Endless Forms Most Beautiful (instrumental); The Long Walk inside them. See docs/cuts/02-endless-forms-most-beautiful.md. Its picture is a fan compilation (same provenance question as act VI, #55).
_acts.III: mrbobbytables — the August 2026 contributors piece, cut from the Curse of Osiris opening cinematic. Owner-named and owner-placed. He calls it PARTIALLY COMPLETE, so it is placed as-is and will be replaced by its finished version.
_acts.IV: kat — Kat Cosgrove's Guardian intro, behind the owner-authored BIAS FOR ACTION slide.
_acts.V: nat — Natali Vlatko's Guardian arrival, behind the same authorisation slide retitled WRONG PLACE, WRONG TIME, RIGHT ATTITUDE.
_acts.VI: 7daystothewolves — the musical. Editorial pass, delivered for review, not approved: provenance is unresolved (issue #55). Its tail plates the Cayde-6 reveal and three gold credits.

_audio: Every act carries its own audio, unprocessed: no normaliser, no limiter, no EQ. The programme is 48 kHz STEREO because that is what the masters are -- every -hq master in Prod is stereo FLAC. The older, now-retired UPLOAD copies were AAC 5.1, but that 5.1 was the same two channels plus a derived LFE (FC/BL/BR digital silence), added by each cut's own run script. Upmixing here to recreate it would be assembly inventing a soundfield, which the audio tenet forbids; if 5.1 delivery is wanted, it belongs in the per-cut scripts that already do it. Only the six act slides are silent; a bed under them is a licensing decision.
_transitions: Issue #105, measured on v0.6 with tools/transitions.py (all times programme clock): every act entered DRY out of the slides' digital silence (4-14 s of -inf per join), the worst being act VII at -15.3 dB one second after the slide, and acts I and III ended HOT against the silence (-24.4 and -14.8 dB in their last second). The treatment below is explicit afade shapes, stated here so they are reproducible: fade_in 2.0 s on every act that starts behind a slide, fade_out 2.0 s on the acts whose tails do not already fade (I, III, V) and 3.0 s on act VII so the programme lands rather than stops. Acts II and VI fade themselves out (measured -96.7 / -90.3 dB in their last seconds) and carry no fade_out; the IV->V join is direct and continuous (-15.2 -> -11.9 dB) and carries no fade on either side. All fade times are ACT FILM time -- the clip's own clock -- so a re-order never moves them. LEFT TO THE OWNER (automatable: no): (1) whether the slides carry a bed or room tone -- a licensing decision, per the megacut skill; (2) levelling the act ENTRIES, which still differ by ~20 dB (act III at -29.5 vs act VII at -15.3) -- static gain per act is a mix decision; (3) how long the slides' silence should be -- the 15 s IV-V slide is deliberate pacing.

_sources._where: Every act plays from ~/Videos/Wolves/Prod, which holds the HIGHEST-QUALITY master of each: FLAC audio and the un-re-encoded picture. They are hardlinks to the per-project masters, so Prod costs no extra disk and cannot drift from what its project built. The retired ~/Videos/UPLOAD staging folder held lossy copies of the same cuts and is NOT what this reads; its removal is issue #81. Act VII's master was re-rendered 2026-08-13 under the new master gate (tools/peaks.py trim, #130) and now measures -1.1 dBTP, inside the -0.9..-1.1 band -- the +0.3 dBTP clip of #82 is fixed in the delivered file; the issue stays open for its owner to close.

items._plates: Act VI carries stories/06-wolves-cayde-plates.json burned in (tools/plate.py burn --fit-picture). Prod holds ONE file per act, hardlinked to its project master, so Prod/06 -> ~/Videos/wolves-musical/wolves-7days-plated-master-v2.mp4. The UN-PLATED v2 master is kept beside it as wolves-7days-master-v2.mp4, because burning is not idempotent: a re-burn starts from the clean file and never stacks a second card on the first. v2 re-burned the tail plates at +10.811 s film time (the manifest's _shifted records it) and the act runs 443.5 s, so slide VII and act VII move +10.811 s of programme time.

_chapters: Each act slide carries the audience-facing `chapter` title; `python3 tools/megacut.py <plan> --chapters` derives the timestamps from this plan's own clock, so the markers can never drift from the running order. The numeral is part of the title because the show is told in numbered acts. Act VIII has no film, so it has no marker -- a chapter that jumps to the next act's footage would be a lie about what plays.
_version: v0.8 -- v0.7 with TWO act changes, sequenced so neither raced the other: (1) act II rebuilt for #98 (PR #136): the TOC exchange (laid out around The Long Walk), the endgame timed cues, the closing quotes over the black outro, and the letterbox callout. Act II's own duration is UNCHANGED (307.998 s -- the picture was re-plated, never re-cut), so no chapter before act VI moves. (2) act VI promoted to its #104 interruption build (PR #135's v2, delivered alongside v1 and promoted here): the Ambassadors interruption adds +10.811 s (432.7 -> 443.5 s film), so slide VII and act VII move +10.811 s; the hold-music slot is deliberately silent pending the owner's licensing call (#104). Planned total 1232.659 s (20:32.7). v0.7 was v0.6 plus the act-join treatment of #105: explicit afade shapes per act (see _transitions), applied at the segment encode, no gain anywhere. v0.6 was v0.5 plus act VI's tail plates (the Cayde-6 reveal and three gold credits). v0.5 was the owner's name for the build before them: everything that exists, assembled, and explicitly NOT the feature. Seven of the eight acts play. What makes it a .5 rather than a 1.0: act VIII (the credits) is not designed (#51), so the programme ends on Europa, and the only names in it are act VI's tail; act VI is an editorial pass whose provenance is an open owner decision (#55); act II's picture comes from a fan compilation with the same question (#74's film); and act III is partially complete by the owner's own description. None of those is fixed by re-assembling -- assembly joins finished things and never re-cuts one.
